The statute will most likely be declared unconstitutional because the 7% signature requirement for independent candidates and political body nominees is excessively burdensome and severely restricts ballot access, violating the First and Fourteenth Amendment rights of association and voting. The 180-day circulation period is also unusually short and, combined with the high signature threshold, creates an insurmountable barrier for candidates outside the two established parties. Such discriminatory ballot access laws fail the balancing test established in Anderson v. Celebrezze and related ballot-access precedents.
